previous_description: Routable grouping of components (a complete user experience)
definition: A top-level UI surface (page, screen, modal, dialog, drawer, panel or overlay) that composes component instances and sub-views into one complete display unit. It is either the target of a navigation route or opened as a standalone surface, not embedded as a fragment within another view.

distinguish_from.when: the fragment is rendered inside a parent view's region, cannot be shown on its own, and has no route or independent open/close lifecycle.
the grouping is a reusable, non-routable composition unit meant to be embedded in many views rather than a destination screen.
the element describes an entire experience (a set of views and its state machine) rather than one screen within it.
the code is a generic modal, drawer or dialog widget definition with props and slots, not a specific application screen built from it.

standard_reference: HTML 5.3 §4.3 Sections (body/main document content) and §4.11.4 The dialog element
code_evidence: A component or template file registered as the target of a router entry, for example a React Router <Route element={...}>, a Next.js app/**/page.tsx, a Vue Router `component:` entry, or an Angular Routes `component` property.
A server-side controller action that renders a full template or page (Django render(request, 'orders/list.html'), Rails `render :index`, a Spring MVC @Controller method returning a view name).

A file under a pages/, views/, screens/ or modals/ directory, or a mobile Activity, Fragment or UIViewController destination in a navigation graph, that sets a page or dialog title and mounts several child components.

attribute_descriptions.name: title
attribute_descriptions.description: Human-readable title shown to users for this view, typically the document <title>, page heading, or dialog header; set it whenever the screen displays or announces a title.

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text summary of the view's purpose and main content for modellers and reviewers; set it when the name and title alone do not convey what the screen is for.

attribute_descriptions.name: routable
attribute_descriptions.description: True when the view can be reached directly through a URL or navigation route; false for views such as modals or overlays that only open programmatically from another view.

attribute_descriptions.name: layout
attribute_descriptions.description: Identifier or name of the layout template or shell (e.g. 'two-column', 'dashboard-shell') this view renders within; set it when the view uses a named layout, and prefer an applies relationship to a ux.layoutconfig for formal binding.

notes: Definition says 'routable', yet the routable boolean allows false; clarify that non-routable modals are still views. 'A complete user experience' collides with ux.uxspec. The free-text layout attribute duplicates the applies/uses relationships to ux.layoutconfig. aggregates and composes to ux.subview are redundant. The source object needs a schema (path, symbol, repository).
